title: Urban Beekeeping
text:
Urban beekeeping has grown rapidly in cities over the past decade. Many residents now keep hives on rooftops, balconies and school grounds. According to the report, city gardens offer bees a wider variety of flowers than intensive farmland does. Supporters argue that this helps pollinators survive during periods when rural crops are scarce.

However, the researchers warned that too many hives in a small area can leave bees competing for the same food. Some local councils have therefore introduced rules limiting the number of colonies per site. Experts also stress that beekeepers must be trained, since untreated diseases can spread quickly between hives. As a result, many cities now offer free courses to new keepers.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what do city gardens offer bees compared with intensive farmland?
According to paragraph two, what problem do researchers warn about when there are too many hives?
options: Bees competing for the same food

questions.text: What can be inferred about rural crops from paragraph one?
options: They are sometimes scarce during certain periods
They are grown only on rooftops
They are protected by local councils

questions.text: Why do some councils limit the number of colonies per site?
options: To reduce the cost of honey
To prevent competition for food among bees
To increase the number of schools

vocabulary.definition: involving a large amount of effort, resources or production in a small area
animals, such as bees, that carry pollen between flowers
trying to get or achieve something that another person or animal also wants
not given medical care or chemical treatment

paragraph_translations: La apicultura urbana ha crecido rápidamente en las ciudades durante la última década. Muchos vecinos tienen ahora colmenas en azoteas, balcones y patios escolares. Según el informe, los jardines urbanos ofrecen a las abejas una variedad de flores mayor que la de las tierras de cultivo intensivo. Quienes lo defienden sostienen que esto ayuda a los polinizadores a sobrevivir en los periodos en que escasean los cultivos rurales.

Sin embargo, los investigadores advirtieron que demasiadas colmenas en una zona pequeña pueden hacer que las abejas compitan por la misma comida. Algunos ayuntamientos han introducido, por tanto, normas que limitan el número de colonias por lugar. Los expertos también insisten en que los apicultores deben recibir formación, ya que las enfermedades sin tratar pueden propagarse rápidamente entre las colmenas. Como consecuencia, muchas ciudades ofrecen ahora cursos gratuitos a los nuevos apicultores.
